## Override any prompt and re-run the whole pipeline on your servers.

A cardiologist with no coding background spots a wrong diagnosis, rewrites the faulty prompt from the dashboard, and re-runs the agent until the answer is right. The developer ships the proven prompt.

## Developers build the pipeline and domain experts tune it.

An engineer can wire up the agent, but they can't judge a sound medical diagnosis or a legally airtight clause. Agent Doctor gives the people who can a dashboard to iterate on prompts and parameters, while the developer keeps ownership of the code.

### Builds the pipeline

Writes the agent code, connects to databases, sets up tools, deploys to production.

### Adds two lines & a webhook

Drops in the SDK and one webhook handler for re-runs. Back to building features.

### Reviews & ships

When the domain expert finds a winning prompt, the dev reviews it and ships it with the next release.

### Sees every step visually

Opens the dashboard, sees the full pipeline trace. Every prompt, every output, every decision the agent made.

### Tweaks prompts & parameters

Spots a bad prompt, rewrites it in plain English. Adjusts the temperature. Hits "Run". No code, no deploys.

### Iterates until it's right

Compares runs side-by-side, uses Probe to debug, runs consistency checks. All from the dashboard.

## Your existing code. Unchanged.

Two lines to capture. One webhook handler to re-run. Agent Doctor hooks into LLM SDKs, vector databases and tool calls at the library level, so your agent logic stays exactly as-is.

# Add these two lines, that's it import agent_doctor agent_doctor. init (api_key= "sk-proj-..." ) # Your existing agent logic, unchanged # LLM calls, vector DB queries and tool calls are auto-captured def handle_ticket (query, customer_id): # LLM call → auto-captured intent = openai.chat.completions. create ( model= "gpt-4o" , messages=[ { "role" : "user" , "content" : query } ] ) # Vector DB lookup → auto-captured docs = pinecone_index. query (vector= embed (query), top_k= 5 ) # Tool call → auto-captured policy = check_refund_policy (customer_id) # LLM call → auto-captured response = openai.chat.completions. create ( model= "gpt-4o" , messages=[ { "role" : "system" , "content" : f"Docs: {docs} Policy: {policy} " }, { "role" : "user" , "content" : query } ] ) return response # Your webhook handler. payload is the run Agent Doctor sends. def on_run (payload): with agent_doctor. run_context (run_id=payload.run_id, overrides=payload.overrides): result = handle_ticket (payload.query, payload.customer_id) # Every step auto-captured. Overrides auto-injected. Done.

- 01 The dashboard sends the override A new prompt, model or temperature for one node, posted to your webhook.

- 02 Your servers run the agent run_context injects the override at runtime. No code change, no redeploy, full access to your private data and tools.

- 03 Only the trace comes back Inputs, outputs and timings for each step land in the dashboard to compare.

Two lines in, every step of your pipeline is in the dashboard.

## Probe finds the broken node by asking you a few questions.

Tell it what the agent should have said and what it said instead. It walks the trace with you, asking three or four plain-English questions, and names the exact step that caused the failure. No logs, no code, no debugging skills needed.

- A chat, so anyone on the team can run it

- Checks the pipeline by halves, so it needs only a few questions

- Highlights the broken node in the trace

- Hands the fix straight to the prompt optimizer

## Consistency checks find the step that answers differently every time.

Run your pipeline ten times with identical input. Per-node consistency scores show exactly which step is non-deterministic, and an AI report tells you why.

- Per-node consistency scores and decision divergence

- AI root cause report with a suggested fix

- Apply the fix, re-test, and verify from the same screen

## The optimizer writes, tests and ranks better prompts for you.

Pick a node and define what "good" looks like. The optimizer generates prompt variants, runs them against your examples, and ranks the results. It starts with GEPA, a genetic strategy that evolves prompts across generations, with more strategies on the way.

- Evolves prompts across generations and keeps the fittest

- Rephrases, expands, compresses and recombines winning traits

- Ranks every variant by its score on your examples, with token cost weighed in

- Shows the winning prompt side by side with the original prompt

## Why not just use a regular observability tool?

Most LLM tracing platforms run experiments on their own cloud, so your agent can't reach your private databases, RAG, or internal tools during a test. They also keep prompt iteration locked behind code, leaving your domain experts out.
